title: Mark Cuban Sold For $5.7 Billion Then Protected It
hook_text: HE SOLD AT THE TOP, THEN HEDGED

beats.say: In nineteen ninety nine, Mark Cuban sold his company for five point seven billion dollars, paid entirely in stock.
beats.visual: a sealed leather briefcase on a polished desk beside a single glowing lamp, no people

beats.say: The buyer was Yahoo, and every dollar of it depended on Yahoo's share price.
beats.visual: a tall stack of paper stock certificates tied with string under a green banker lamp, no people

beats.say: That meant his fortune could shrink if the price fell.
beats.visual: a glass hourglass with sand running out on a dark table, hard side light

beats.say: And the price was sky high, in the middle of a tech bubble.
beats.visual: a giant soap bubble floating over a dark city skyline at dusk, no people

beats.say: Most people who get rich in stock just hold it and hope. Hope is not a plan when a fortune is tied to one price.
beats.visual: a lone figure standing under a flickering streetlamp in the rain, silhouette

beats.say: So what did Cuban do instead?
beats.visual: a brass compass resting on an old map in dim light, close-up

beats.say: He has said he used hedges, which are contracts that pay off if his Yahoo shares drop.
beats.visual: an old steel safe door slowly closing in a dark vault, thin light along the edge

beats.say: Then Yahoo's stock fell by more than ninety percent from its peak.
beats.visual: a steep snowy cliff face disappearing into clouds, wide shot, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Making a gain and keeping a gain are two different jobs.
beats.visual: a hand holding a single gold coin over a deep dark well, close-up, no face

beats.say: Protecting a gain can mean selling some, spreading it out, or paying for insurance like that.
beats.visual: a row of sturdy wooden umbrellas open in a heavy storm, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: hedging costs money, it caps your upside, and looking back always feels easy. Nobody knows the top in advance.
beats.visual: a quiet empty road in thick fog with faint headlights far away, no people

beats.say: Do not copy a billionaire's trade. Copy the question: what happens if this goes wrong?
beats.visual: a lone lantern glowing on a dark wooden dock at night, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

description: In 1999 Mark Cuban sold Broadcast.com to Yahoo for about 5.7 billion dollars in stock, then reportedly hedged his Yahoo shares before the dot-com crash. What protecting a gain means, and the honest catch.
first_comment: Would you have sold, or held on? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: 1999: Yahoo bought Broadcast.com for about $5.7B in stock
Cuban has said he hedged his Yahoo shares with collars and puts
Yahoo stock fell roughly 90%+ from its 2000 peak by 2001-02
Catch: hedging costs money and limits upside; hindsight is easy
